newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin appoints Security Council troubleshooter.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin appoints Security Council troubleshooter.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin appointed Boris Agapov, a leading politician from the troubled North Caucasus region, as a deputy secretary of his policy-making Security Council on Monday, the Kremlin press service said.
Agapov is vice-president of Ingushetia, a region bordering Chechnya, and has played a significant role in the peace process there, including securing the release of prisoners.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Security Council spokesman Igor Ignatyev as saying Agapov, 51, would use his experience as a troubleshooter to handle crisis management for the council.
The former border guard general would also deal with matters relating to frontier security.
Ignatyev said Agapov had been involved in the freeing of several journalists held hostage in Chechnya recently.

There are five other deputy secretaries of the Security Council, who work under secretary Ivan Rybkin. Of these, the best known is business magnate Boris Berezovsky, who played a high-profile role in securing last month's peace deal between Moscow and the separatist leadership in Chechnya.
